source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. STM origins and dynamic transactions were checked against Shavit-Touitou and Herlihy et al.; opacity against Guerraoui-Kapalka; the versioned ownership path against TL2; composition against Harris et al. and current GHC STM documentation; global validation design against NOrec; durable foundations against Larus-Rajwar and Herlihy-Shavit; and the distinction between STM and hardware transactional fallback against current Intel documentation. Five ACM DOI targets returned publisher HTTP 403 to automated curl after DOI resolution, but bibliographic metadata and scoped claims were independently checked through indexed publisher records. The five remaining publisher or official documentation targets resolved directly. No inaccessible quotation or implementation detail is relied upon.

evidence: Definitions and Notation consistently defines transaction T, read and write sets R(T) and W(T), begin and commit timestamps, versions, conflicts, sequential and concurrent histories, real-time precedence, and state invariant I(s).

The chapter distinguishes transaction from attempt, abstract state from metadata, committed value from tentative value, automatic conflict abort from semantic retry, and serializability from strict serializability and opacity.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Checked set intersections, version comparisons, timestamp names, state/history terminology, all-or-nothing publication language, and every use of guarantee, mechanism, policy, proof, model, and empirical evidence.

evidence: Recomputed the executable trace: T2 changes (5,5) to (3,7), stale T1 aborts without publication, retry changes (3,7) to (2,8), and the sum remains ten at every committed state.
artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-061/report.json records exact values (3,7) after conflict, (2,8) after retry, final sum ten, per-location version two, empty stderr, and zero exit code.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The program is a deterministic sequential validation model. Its dictionary updates are not machine-atomic and it does not numerically establish opacity, weak-memory correctness, liveness, or production performance.

evidence: For a transfer delta, (x - delta) + (y + delta) simplifies to x + y, so an atomic committed transfer preserves the stated sum invariant.
The conflict expression includes write-write, T-write/U-read, and U-write/T-read intersections; read-read overlap alone is excluded.

The commit argument requires exclusive publication rights for W(T), validation of every dependency in R(T), one permitted serialization point, and reader ordering wholly before or after the transaction.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Symbolic checks support the chapter's teaching derivations; they are not a mechanized proof of TL2, another STM implementation, or a host-language memory model.

evidence: Reviewed read-only, write-only, duplicate/read-own-write, empty and large access sets; real versus false conflicts; eager/lazy detection and versioning; visible/invisible reads; single/multi-version state; metadata wrap; and partial publication.

Reviewed inconsistent doomed reads, nontransactional access, privatization, speculative pointers, reclamation, GC retention, exceptions, asynchronous cancellation, flattened/closed/open nesting, long transactions, starvation, overload, fallback, shutdown, restart, signals, foreign code, and adversarial retries.
Reviewed I/O, file/cache mutation, time/random inputs, logs, effect intents, crash windows, HTM capacity and spurious aborts, and high-consequence physical actuation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The boundary audit covers semantic, representation, memory, effect, progress, resource, lifecycle, operational, security, and safety boundaries rather than only normal successful commits.

evidence: Uncommitted writes remain private; an abort changes no abstract transactional state; a commit exposes one complete write set; and readers cannot accept an intermediate write-set prefix.

Every accepted read belongs to a legal consistent snapshot, every semantic dependency is validated, ownership and waiter metadata are released on terminal paths, and transactional/plain access obeys one declared discipline.
The sum-ten trace and worked transfer preserve the application invariant across committed states while deliberately rejecting the stale attempt.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked invariants across begin, transactional read, read-own-write, buffer, conflict, ownership, validation, serialization, publication, abort, retry, exception, cancellation, effect dispatch, and shutdown.

evidence: The representation argument separates stable committed value/version state from valid ownership descriptors and prohibits aborted descriptors from later publishing.
The read-validity argument pairs value and metadata observations and requires incremental or snapshot protection so doomed transactions do not operate on a fractured state.
The commit, abort, and progress arguments explicitly list premises, concrete-to-abstract obligations, cleanup, and scheduler/allocator/primitive/fallback assumptions.
proof_review.notes: Reviewed as proof structure and obligations, not as a complete formal proof for a named implementation. The text explicitly requires an algorithm-specific serialization point and precise opacity model.

evidence: The chapter labels the executable code a sequential teaching model and states that it does not implement concurrent STM, arbitrary-interleaving opacity, atomic publication, or a language memory model.
Correctness-condition definitions, TL2-style mechanism, representation and refinement obligations, contention policy, empirical adoption evidence, and named human review are kept distinct.
Hardware transactions, database durability, strong atomicity, weak atomicity, and external exactly-once behavior are explicitly prevented from inheriting STM claims without added protocols.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No example, test, DOI, runtime API, or internal review is presented as universal proof, durability, production certification, or external academic/practitioner approval.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-061 passed one annotated Python model with a recorded Python version, source, command, exact stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit code.

The adoption section separately requires bounded/model histories, adversarial schedules, differential reference tests, race/undefined-behavior tools, faults, representative workloads, oversubscription, NUMA, shutdown, observability, and alternative baselines.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The reproduced trace establishes only its stated deterministic behavior; it provides no production throughput, tail latency, fairness, progress, memory-model, durability, security, or safety evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed sequential specification, histories and opacity, metadata, lazy optimistic commit, design dimensions, effects, semantic retry, exceptions/cancellation/nesting, mixed accesses, progress, operations, evidence, alternatives, and failure modes for consistency and scope.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed metadata granularity, version wrap, write acquisition, partial publication, effect deferral and idempotency, crash windows, fallback coordination, access discipline, privatization/reclamation, telemetry, admission, overload, shutdown, current GHC semantics, HTM distinction, and deployment evidence.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet foregrounds consistency and effect boundaries; exposition progresses from abstract contract through correctness, mechanism, operational use, and evidence; the executable trace is bounded honestly; ten examples are distinct; and five exercises progress from definitions to railway transfer with complete matching answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external STM, concurrency-theory, formal-methods, database, Haskell/GHC, compiler, architecture, Intel/HTM, performance, security, medical, railway, regulatory, operational, or safety review is claimed. The chapter and model establish neither a named STM implementation's opacity, memory-order correctness, progress, resource bounds, durability, effect safety, benchmark benefit, deployment suitability, nor physical-system safety.
